challenge.reason: The old decision rested on two stated premises: fewer than 20 issues per run, and single-file simplicity for atomic writes. Both have changed. Runs now admit 200+ issues, and the concurrency executor writes many issues in parallel, which puts every status write and heartbeat behind one lock and lets one corrupt byte lose the whole run. Per-issue files remove the shared lock and limit a corrupt write to one issue. The directory root is unchanged and an index file keeps discovery working. The supersession argument holds. Implementation should make index updates atomic so the index cannot drift from the per-issue files.
